nodes.label: PHASES.md Build Tracker
nodes.rationale: Checkbox tracker plus an append-only Session Log; the next session reads it to know where to resume, so it must be committed before a session ends.

nodes.label: Phase 0 - Foundations
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a runnable but NOT-yet-trading skeleton: all common plumbing and continuity files first, no live orders and no real strategy, so the exit criterion is 'boots on testnet, reconciles cleanly' rather than any P&L.

nodes.label: Phase 1 - Crypto Long-term
nodes.rationale: 1D timeframe, 5x leverage, top-5 by Delta India 24h volume, Kelly-sized against a Rs 50k bucket. Exit criterion is 14 clean testnet days under the new bucket structure plus a clean first live week.

nodes.label: Phase 1a - Bucket framework (Decisions 013-017)
nodes.rationale: One shared engine library driven by many per-bucket configs; the old src/strategies/crypto_longterm was deleted and re-ported so there is exactly one code path.

nodes.label: Phase 1b - Soak restart on new structure
nodes.rationale: Soak clock arguably restarts from 2026-07-07 because the Phase 1c safety changes landed then. Go-live is BLOCKED on backtester-derived mu/sigma, which is a separate user-built project.

nodes.label: Phase 1c - Review backlog (Decision 021)
nodes.rationale: Output of a full-project critical review on 2026-07-06; worked strictly top-to-bottom in priority order so a 'continue' always has an unambiguous next item.

nodes.label: Phase 2 - Crypto Swing
nodes.rationale: Provisioning sequence matters: sub-account API keys must exist BEFORE the bucket is enabled, because missing DELTA_SWING_* creds fail the whole bot at boot by design.

nodes.label: Phase 4-interim - Blasting Momentum swing bridge (Dhan sandbox)
nodes.rationale: A standalone runner in scripts/dhan-scanner/ deliberately OUTSIDE the deterministic bot loop (no Postgres, kill switch, idempotent ids or audit rows), to be RETIRED once the real Dhan adapter lands. Open risks: interactive-logon Task Scheduler jobs, backtest universe (Nifty 500) narrower than live (all NSE+BSE), and no protective stop vs Decision 022.

nodes.label: Phase 4 - Midcap-150 1h Mean Reversion (LIVE 2026-07-27)
nodes.rationale: Planned around the TRAIN fold grade (~PF 2.3, ~+25%/yr on margin), NOT the holdout's +57%, because the holdout is crash-boosted and corrections should be treated as upside rather than the base case. Run at quarter scale: 5 slots x Rs 10k instead of 20, so expect roughly a quarter of the backtest's rupee P&L.

nodes.label: Phase 4b - Stocks Intraday (intraday-indian)
nodes.rationale: NIFTY-100 gap-down reversal, planned around the HOLDOUT grade (~PF 1.7, ~+13%/yr on margin). Ships DARK (enabled:false) pending user review; regime gate deliberately OFF because the strategy fades panic and the holdout profit IS the Apr-2025 crash.

nodes.label: Phase 7a - Live-session supervision (Decision 033)
nodes.rationale: Three tiers with authority DECREASING as intelligence increases. A PROCESS watchdog beside the equity watchdog, added because breakers only ask 'has equity fallen off a cliff', which is right for leveraged crypto and wrong for Indian equity where failures happen at healthy equity.

nodes.label: Tier 1 - Deterministic session invariants
nodes.rationale: Shipped OBSERVE-ONLY first (pages with an '[OBSERVE-ONLY, would have HALTED]' prefix) with streaks still counting so flipping needs no warm-up; enforcing flipped on 2026-08-01 after 4 clean sessions, with the honest caveat recorded that those sessions held zero positions so 4 of 6 checks were vacuous.

nodes.label: Tier 2 - Intraday supervisor agent (designed, not built)
nodes.rationale: Hard-constrained to never call the Dhan API (a second session evicts the bot's token) and never to run on the bot VM (a dead VM would silence its own watchdog). Authority capped at L1 halt on a defined whitelist, then page.

nodes.label: Tier 3 - EOD session postmortem
nodes.rationale: Runs 15:45 IST, AFTER the 15:15 square-off and 15:30 close, so anything still open genuinely IS carried overnight. The nightly Parquet export is an ARCHIVE, not a REPORT: it says what was traded, nothing about whether the session behaved.

nodes.label: buckets.yaml (per-bucket capital, leverage, stops, cadence)
nodes.rationale: Single git-tracked file carrying capital_inr, leverage, stop_loss_pct, entry windows and tick_interval_seconds per bucket, so enabling/disabling a bucket is a config push rather than a code change.

nodes.label: BucketRunner pipeline orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Step 0 is the exit engine, run for every strategy INCLUDING gate-blocked ones, so a regime gate can never trap an open position.

nodes.label: Kill switch (DB row, blocks risk-increasing actions only)
nodes.rationale: Decision 024: killed means risk-INCREASING actions are blocked, not everything. Strategy exits still run reduce-only via allow_when_killed and breakers keep watching, because a halted account with open positions still needs flattening. kill_switch.disengage() has exactly ONE caller (the dashboard button), so nothing clears a halt automatically.

nodes.label: Equity breakers (daily DD, liquidation distance, funding extreme)
Breaker enforcement (trip -> kill switch + flatten)
nodes.rationale: FLATTEN lives here and is reachable ONLY by a deterministic breaker trip; nothing intelligent may close a position.

nodes.label: Authority ladder - supervision may HALT, only breakers may FLATTEN
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing design decision of Decision 033: engaging a kill switch is risk-REDUCING and reversible, closing a position is a trading decision. Capping enforcement at HALT is what keeps House Rule #1 (no LLM in the trading loop) intact when the Tier 2 LLM supervisor lands.

nodes.label: Exchange-resident protective stop sweep (Decision 022)
nodes.rationale: Self-healing per-tick sweep: places missing stops, resizes on adds, cancels orphans. Stops flow through OrderManager so a stop that fires while the bot is DOWN still gets P&L-paired by the reconciler. Trigger is mark price snapped to live tick_size.

nodes.label: src/safety/session_invariants.py - six process checks
nodes.rationale: Runs once per 60s tick per account AFTER the stop sweep, so 'no stop' means the sweep FAILED rather than that it has not run yet. effective_holdings INTERSECTS the Trade ledger with exchange positions: the ledger alone goes stale when Dhan auto-square-off closes a position without writing a SELL row, while positions alone cannot tell the bot's rows from the user's on a shared account.

nodes.label: squareoff invariant (HALT)
nodes.rationale: The square-off lives inside the STRATEGY exit and the Decision 031 CNC fallback has no broker net behind it, so a stale feed or rejected exit silently turns a 5x intraday trade into an overnight delivery. Nothing asserted this before Decision 033.

nodes.label: stop_coverage invariant (HALT, 2-tick sustain)
nodes.rationale: Two-tick sustain because one uncovered reading can race a just-placed stop.

nodes.label: bucket_liveness invariant (NOTICE, per-bucket heartbeat)
nodes.rationale: The process heartbeat keeps beating for the other buckets, so it structurally cannot see ONE wedged bucket; a bucket:<id> row per bucket can.

nodes.label: foreign_positions invariant (NOTICE, never acted on)
nodes.rationale: Makes Decision 027 ownership scoping visible without acting; it is violated continuously while the user holds anything on the shared Dhan account, which is what forced the digest-based alert dedup.

nodes.label: scan_coverage invariant (NOTICE) - watches perception, not positions
nodes.rationale: First invariant to watch PERCEPTION rather than positions: attempting 0 of a non-empty configured universe, or evaluating 0 of a non-empty attempted one, is a blind scanner. Downgraded from HALT to NOTICE the next day because a blind scanner already enters nothing, so halting prevents nothing while stranding the bucket overnight (disengage has one caller, the dashboard button). A payload without counts reads UNKNOWN, never zero.

nodes.label: signal_delivery invariant (NOTICE)
nodes.rationale: Pages when a signal the strategy DID produce could not be sized because the broker price fetch failed. Matched on the constant rather than a substring, pinned by a test, since a reworded literal would silently disarm the alarm.

nodes.label: data_ failure vs allocator decision - reasons must be distinguishable
nodes.rationale: The recurring root defect of this project: a data FAILURE and a deliberate DECISION recorded identically. The scanner learned it in Decision 033 (data_-prefixed outcomes, outcome histogram, one snapshot row per evaluated symbol), the sizer had not (PRICE_FETCH_FAILED_REASON vs NO_MARK_PRICE_REASON vs skipped_other), and the intraday cache learned it again (could-not-evaluate is not did-not-qualify, so an all-data_-reason pass must not be cached as the day's answer).

nodes.label: INVARIANT_VIOLATED audit event + digest-keyed alert dedup
nodes.rationale: Invariants paged Telegram but wrote NO audit row, so since the EOD journal is built entirely from audit rows, every violation that cleared before halting was reported as 'nothing tripped'. Alerts are now keyed on a digest of what would be SAID (would_halt included, so escalation still pages; alert_signature lets a self-moving detail like a growing age be excluded), replacing an hourly re-arming dedup that produced ~72 msgs/day.

nodes.label: Heartbeat / dead-man's switch
nodes.rationale: The watchdog runs on Railway while the bot runs on the VM, precisely so a dead VM cannot silence its own alarm.

nodes.label: Daily-anchored drawdown breaker (Decision 023)
nodes.rationale: Snapshots each sub-account's equity at the first breaker pass of the UTC day so check_daily_drawdown becomes pure anchor-vs-current math and REALIZED losses count toward the trip, which a wallet-only comparison misses.

nodes.label: net_owned() bot-ownership scoping on shared accounts
nodes.rationale: Bot-owned = the bot's own net-long trades (buys minus executed sells, windowed). Gates three paths on a shared_account flag: reconciler orphan-import (the linchpin, since the exit engine runs off DB Position rows), the stop sweep (never cancels the user's resting stops), and breakers (drawdown measured on capital+own-unrealized so the user's P&L cannot trip the bot's flatten). Crypto is unaffected - sub-accounts are exclusively the bot's per Decision 019.

nodes.label: Shared Dhan account hazard (2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: One Dhan account holds both the bot's positions and the user's manual trades, so any component that reads THE ACCOUNT and calls it THE BOT is a live-money hazard. The same failure mode recurred three times: the reconciler orphan-importing NIFTY option legs, the EOD report claiming Rs 21,479 of the user's notional as carried overnight, and the dashboard home route rendering orphan rows as the bot's.

nodes.label: src/order_manager/pnl.py - cumulative and per-trade P&L math
nodes.rationale: Basis is synced wallet equity minus capital_inr minus manual capital_adjustments_inr, so deposits and withdrawals do not read as P&L. Indian buckets later switched to bucket_ledger_pnl off their own Trade rows because the shared Dhan wallet double-counted across buckets.

nodes.label: Fills / fees / realized-P&L ingestion
nodes.rationale: Reduce-only exits are paired with entries for realized P&L net of BOTH sides' fees; contract size is read live from /v2/products rather than trusted from YAML.

nodes.label: src/reporting/eod.py - EOD session report
nodes.rationale: Postgres ONLY, never the Dhan API (a second session evicts the bot's token). Three outputs from one source: Telegram digest, session_report row, /journal route. A quiet day says so plainly instead of rendering an empty skeleton, because a report that looks broken on a normal day is one you stop reading. After the 08-04/05 outage it carries the configured->attempted->evaluated funnel and refuses the word 'quiet' unless something was evaluated.

nodes.label: Signals seen but NOT taken, grouped by reason
nodes.rationale: Reads sizing_snapshot, which had held that record since Decision 026 and which nothing had ever read back; it is the literal answer to 'why didn't it trade today?'.

nodes.label: src/reporting/slippage.py - decision-lag vs execution slippage
nodes.rationale: Three prices split the gap into two costs with COMPLETELY DIFFERENT FIXES: decision lag (scan latency / tick cadence) and execution (spread + impact + order type). Sign convention makes positive ALWAYS a cost on both sides of the book so entries and exits do not cancel into a comforting zero.

nodes.label: signal_price + decision_price on Trade.extra
nodes.rationale: What the strategy SAW is not something the exchange knows, so it is unrecoverable unless recorded at the moment of decision - every unrecorded day was live evidence permanently lost with two buckets already on real money. Exits get decision_price only, because select_exits returns bare symbols and there is no per-symbol reference bar without changing that contract for every strategy.

nodes.label: backtest_baseline in allocator.yaml (live-vs-backtest edge)
nodes.rationale: Purely descriptive and THE SIZER NEVER READS IT, so House Rule 7 holds. PF and win rate are scale-invariant, which is what makes a live rupee figure comparable to a backtest on unlevered returns. Both baselines must come from ONE fold each - they previously mixed folds and benchmarked against a composite run that never existed. Two honesty guards: an undefined PF is never printed as infinity, and below 20 closed round-trips the section leads with 'too early to read'.

nodes.label: src/reporting/tax_ledger.py - consolidated trade ledger
nodes.rationale: For RECONCILIATION against the broker statement, never as a filing document. Two traps pinned by test: realized P&L is stamped on BOTH legs of a round-trip so it must be attributed to the CLOSING leg only, and currency is per-broker and NEVER converted since the fixed 85 USD/INR is a sizing convention, not a market rate.

nodes.label: src/shared/scanner/meanrev.py + engine equity_meanrev_1h
nodes.rationale: 09:15-anchored 15m->1h resample (7 bins/session, the last a 15-min stub that IS a real signal bar), EMA20 distance, FRESH -6.5% cross only, adjusted/unadjusted scale guard, prior-close daily ATR14. Caches per 1h bin so a 60s tick costs ~190 Dhan calls per BIN, not per minute, and enforces a <=5-new-entries-per-day budget.

nodes.label: mean_reversion_1h.py Strategy
nodes.rationale: Entry on the freshly-closed bin, mean-touch plus 20-trading-day exits, and it EMITS its own 3.5x-ATR stop distance rather than relying on the bucket net.

nodes.label: Bar-selection bugfix (locate_bin / _through_bin, 2026-08-01)
nodes.rationale: The scanner was structurally incapable of opening a position for its entire first live week. One fact, two consequences: a scan fires at HH:16, one minute AFTER the bin boundary, so Dhan's feed already carries the NEXT in-progress bin. Entries required the wanted bin to be newest (always off by one, every symbol None); exits read iloc[-1] with no pinning (the still-forming bin, the opposite of the docstring). Both now LOCATE the wanted bin and truncate there; ewm(adjust=False) is causal so retained values are bit-identical. A third defect: before 10:15 the previous CALENDAR day was asked for, so a Monday requested a Sunday bin, making the Friday-stub -> Monday-09:15 entry unreachable.

nodes.label: bar_key on scanner_snapshot / daily_universe (migrations 0012, 0013)
nodes.rationale: Rows were keyed (date, strategy_id, symbol) and written delete-then-insert scoped to the DAY - right for a once-a-day screen, destructive for a cut that runs on all 7 bins, so each pass ERASED the previous one and only 15:16 survived. Worst hit was the 09:16 pass, the only one reading the previous session's stub bin. Volume 94 -> 658 rows/day. Migration 0012's own backfill then failed because ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT '' populates existing rows on the spot so WHERE bar_key IS NULL matched nothing; 0013 repairs it, and the server_default STAYS because deploy.sh migrates before it restarts.

nodes.label: scripts/meanrev_1h_parity.py (208/214)
nodes.rationale: Scores the live port against 214 frozen backtest trades on cross, distance and ATR stop. The 6 misses are all the EMA20 warm-up guard at the data boundary, i.e. the port is conservative rather than broken; the score being UNCHANGED at 208/214 after the bar-selection fix is the regression proof.

nodes.label: Strategy-supplied resting stop distances (extra_payload -> Trade.extra)
nodes.rationale: Decision 032: a strategy may supply its own per-position distance which can only ever TIGHTEN against the bucket percent, so the bucket figure remains a fallback net that a strategy can never loosen.

nodes.label: Stop attribution / product / self-recognition fix (2026-08-12)
nodes.rationale: An adversarial review found the first attempt inert; all three defects had to land together. (1) attribution read only Position (written every 5 MIN) while the sweep runs ~9 SEC after a fill, and the Trade fallback's status filter omitted PENDING, the exact state a fresh Dhan order is in. (2) ensure_stop_protection never passed product=, so every stop defaulted to MTF and a reduce-only MTF sell against an INTRADAY long reduces nothing. (3) The sweep could not SEE its own stops (adapter hardcoded reduce_only False), so it planned a fresh stop every 60s - harmless only while every stop was rejected, dangerous the moment MTF consent made them accepted. Recognition is now inferred from trigger price plus OUR correlationId, which Dhan returns only for API orders, so a user-placed stop can never be matched or cancelled.

nodes.label: Dhan MTF consent checkbox blocker (2026-08-11)
nodes.rationale: MTF was enabled on the account, but Dhan requires a separate consent checkbox ticked on a manual App/Web order which API orders cannot tick, so every MTF order swing-indian ever sent was RMS-rejected - the second independent reason it had never filled since going live.

nodes.label: MTF->CNC fallback re-sent the leveraged quantity as cash
nodes.rationale: A live-money hazard found on the way in: ~Rs 38k of cash for a Rs 10k slot, on the account shared with the user's own money. Now capped at 1x like the MIS path, generalising Decision 031's guard.

nodes.label: MTF carry interest on (notional - margin) at 14.6%/yr
nodes.rationale: The backtest omits it and it is ~4% of net, so booking it per calendar day keeps live P&L honest against the baseline.

nodes.label: src/shared/scanner/gap_reversal.py + engine equity_intraday
nodes.rationale: The morning cut runs ONCE per session and caches to DailyUniverse, because re-screening 99 symbols on every 60s tick would recompute a constant.

nodes.label: gap_down_reversal.py Strategy (first reversal candle, 15:15 square-off)
nodes.rationale: Its 15:15 square-off lives inside the strategy exit, which is exactly why the squareoff invariant had to be added as an independent assertion.

nodes.label: src/shared/scanner/patterns.py (TV engulfing_bull + hammer)
nodes.rationale: 1:1 port from TradingView. The parity harness caught that body_avg is a 14-EMA that must run over the FULL multi-session series - session-scoping it reproduced only 33/76, because a gap morning's opening candles inflate the average and kill long_body.

nodes.label: scripts/gap_reversal_parity.py (75/76)
nodes.rationale: Scores gap screen, pattern name AND entry bar time against 76 frozen trades; the single accepted miss is VEDL 2025-08-26, whose daily history is rescaled by a later demerger. Re-run before/after the _MIN_SESSION_BARS change to prove blast radius, verified rather than assumed.

nodes.label: _MIN_SESSION_BARS gate blocked intraday-indian entirely (2026-08-10)
nodes.rationale: Zero daily_universe rows ever: the gate demanded 6 bars (through 09:45) while the screen only reads today[0].open and today[2].close, so every name was rejected data_too_few_session_bars. Set to 4, not 3, because Dhan's 5m response carries the in-progress candle. THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS WRONG: delaying the scan to 09:45 would have amputated the front of a validated entry window, since _MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_BARS=1 makes the 09:25 and 09:30 pattern bars permanently unreachable by then. The empty cut was then cached for the day; rescreen is now retried, bounded at 5/session so it cannot serialise into an hour of scanning and manufacture a 429 storm.

nodes.label: _blasting_momentum.py (made inert)
nodes.rationale: Retired by underscore-prefixing the module and removing its strategy_master row rather than deleting it; configs moved aside to scanner_blasting.yaml / allocator_blasting.yaml so the loader cannot discover it.

nodes.label: Per-bucket / per-coin HMM regime brain
nodes.rationale: Inference and retrain both drop the in-progress candle. The window cache was generalised to any <N><unit> TF because 4h/15m buckets never hit it and were paying a per-tick HMM fit plus snapshot write; the cache is bounded at one entry per (bucket, symbol) rather than growing per bar. Turned OFF for both Indian buckets - the gate removes the crash-rebound trades that ARE the edge.

nodes.label: Kelly allocator / sizer with skip rules
nodes.rationale: Insufficiency is checked against required MARGIN, not leveraged notional (Decision 018). size_positions once ran per-strategy against full capital so two scanner sets could each claim 100%; the runner now threads committed_margin and the budget is capped at min(wallet, capital) per Decision 027.

nodes.label: Per-bucket tick cadence (tick_interval_for_tf)
nodes.rationale: Pipeline passes pace to the bucket TF (tf/20 clamped to [60s, 15min]) while breakers, stop sweep and heartbeat stay on the 60s loop, so slowing the scan never slows safety. swing-indian pins tick_interval_seconds: 60 because a 1d regime model would otherwise have paced a 1h strategy at 900s.

nodes.label: TF-scaled dedup window (dedup_window_hours_for_tf)
nodes.rationale: 23/24 of one strategy bar, so a 1d strategy keeps its 23h window while a 1h strategy gets ~57 min; a fixed 23h window would have blocked every swing entry, which is why this unblocked Phase 2.

nodes.label: Delta client hardening (central _request)
nodes.rationale: Safety-aware retries: GETs retry transport/5xx with backoff; 429 is retried for ALL verbs because rate-limited means never processed; expired-signature errors resync a clock offset from the response Date header; order POSTs NEVER transport-retry because OrderManager's client_order_id recovery owns that.

nodes.label: Google Drive audit_log archive + OAuth
nodes.rationale: The 180-day prune was hard-deleting the forensic record with NO copy behind it, and the mirror had never run once for three independent silent reasons: no credentials set (returned early at INFO), google-* packages in pyproject.toml but not requirements.txt which is what deploy.sh installs, and service-account-only auth which CANNOT work on a personal @gmail.com because a service account has no Drive storage quota.

nodes.label: Contiguous archive watermark guard
nodes.rationale: Retention's audit cutoff is the EARLIER of the 180-day age and an archive watermark, and the watermark only advances CONTIGUOUSLY so one good night cannot bless three months of backlog. Nothing archived implies nothing deleted. The backfill tool itself had the inverse bug: --from combined with force=True would have let a PARTIAL run set a watermark asserting everything below it was archived.

nodes.label: Archive dead-man's switch on the VM tick loop
nodes.rationale: A dead Railway scheduler container stops the archive and every alarm about it in one stroke, so the watcher runs on the VM - the exact mirror of the Railway-side heartbeat watch that exists because a dead VM must not silence its own watchdog. Pinned by a test asserting _check_archive appears in run_bot and NOT in run_scheduler. One symptom (a watermark that stops advancing) covers scheduler down, token expired and upload failing.

nodes.label: Dhan single-session token eviction and mint cooldown
nodes.rationale: Dhan tokens are single-session: a peer process minting invalidates every other process's token SERVER-SIDE while it is still valid by its own JWT timestamp. Original client only retried on HTTP 401 (DH-906 is HTTP 400 in the envelope) and minted before checking the shared cache, producing N-process thrash. Mints are rate-limited to one per ~2 minutes and the refusal arrives as HTTP 200 with the error in the BODY, so raise_for_status() passes it - the cause of the 2026-08-04/05 blind outage (3,831 mint attempts in one day). Fixes: adopt a peer's cached token before minting, record rejected tokens, a real 130s cooldown gate, and a 300s grace because the competing login starts the server-side cooldown.

nodes.label: Two-day blind scan outage (2026-08-04/05)
nodes.rationale: Both live Indian buckets scanned ZERO symbols for two full trading days with no alert, no breaker and no HALT. Every symbol's fetch raised into 'except: continue' so the scan logged 0/0 and the EOD journal said 'nothing qualified'. The only durable trace was two bucket_liveness NOTICEs, fired incidentally because retries made one pass take 2,245s. Cost was zero only because mean reversion produced no signals those days - luck, not design.

nodes.label: client-id: "" on /v2/marketfeed/quote - the real cause of zero fills
nodes.rationale: The quote endpoint authenticates on access-token AND client-id, and the data adapter hardcoded an empty client-id: 76 of 76 calls 401'd and the endpoint had NEVER once succeeded. It hid because the charts endpoints do NOT require client-id, so the SAME token returned 200 thousands of times a day beside the failures. Cost: every mark price comes through this endpoint and no entry can be sized without one, so swing-indian was structurally incapable of opening a position since go-live. It also DROVE the token churn, since get_ticker read 401 as 'token expired' and re-minted forever, and Dhan being single-session each mint evicted the session the other endpoints were using.

nodes.label: Dhan 5 req/s cap - 429 backoff + 0.22s pacing
nodes.rationale: The 09:40 dry run showed 95/99 gap-screen fetches failing 429 because the scan fired ~100/s against a 5 req/s cap - the live bucket would have been half-blind every morning. Caught by a dry run BEFORE any money.

nodes.label: Redaction by parameter NAME, not by value shape
nodes.rationale: Every redaction rule was SHAPE-based (hex >=32, base64 >=40) and a 6-digit Dhan PIN matches none, nor could any value-shaped rule catch it without also redacting prices and security ids - so sensitive query params are redacted by NAME. Earlier the same class of gap put the Telegram bot token in journald in plaintext, because redaction was a structlog-only processor while httpx logs via stdlib.

nodes.label: Live Dhan client id + PIN committed in a public repo fixture
nodes.rationale: In tests/unit/test_dhan_config.py from f03962d in a PUBLIC GitHub repo. The TOTP secret there was the RFC-4226 example value so it was never exposed, and PIN + client_id alone cannot mint an API token, but the PIN is the Dhan LOGIN pin. Scrubbing does not un-publish it; rotation is the user's action and remains outstanding.

nodes.label: Empty runner set exited 0, so systemd never restarted (80-min outage)
nodes.rationale: An 18:00 restart landed inside Dhan's mint cooldown, the startup probe served a rejected token, a broad except disabled the WHOLE Dhan account, both Indian buckets were the only enabled ones, runners was empty, main() returned NORMALLY, and Restart=on-failure treats exit 0 as success - service inactive with NRestarts=0. Fixes: _probe_with_retry on a schedule deliberately SPANNING the 130s cooldown (20/60/70s, pinned by a test asserting the sum > 130) while a permanent fault still fails first attempt; and an empty runner set with buckets ENABLED now raises SystemExit(1) so any unanticipated init failure becomes a retry loop instead of a silently idle box.

nodes.label: Every deploy restarts the bot and is a real risk event
nodes.rationale: Because the Dhan token is single-session and mints are cooldown-limited, a restart can strand the bot. Lesson after four deploys in one day: batch changes into ONE deploy and never deploy near 09:15 or 15:15.

nodes.label: STALE-CLOSE bug - Dhan publishes the daily candle late
nodes.rationale: The official daily candle is absent at 20:50 IST on trade date (probed, not a toDate-exclusivity issue), so the 18:00 prepare computed prev_close and all indicators one session stale and the morning gap fired against a two-session-old close: PPAP's '+12.97% gap' was really -1.8%. Fixed by splicing today's completed session from 15m intraday; the same constraint forced the corporate-action guard to be reformulated for live.

nodes.label: Layer-1 deploy gate (CI green required, pre-restart selfcheck)
nodes.rationale: deploy.sh refuses non-green commits, runs a pre-restart selfcheck entrypoint, and auto-applies alembic migrations when a push touches migrations/ - it migrates BEFORE it restarts, which is why new columns need server_defaults. Day-one catch: tests silently depended on a local .env.

nodes.label: Dhan sandbox edge blocks datacenter IPs
nodes.rationale: From the VM, sandbox.dhan.co 403s pre-auth while api.dhan.co 401s normally, with no DevPortal knob - so the soak split into a local order path and a VM data path. Live cutover is unaffected because live orders go to api.dhan.co. A fail-fast probe makes the bucket skip cleanly rather than erroring every tick.

nodes.label: Multiple named scanner sets per bucket (Decision 026)
nodes.rationale: scanner_<name>.yaml + allocator_<name>.yaml linked by a `scanner` column in strategy_master.csv. Sets run as different strategy NAMES and dedup is per bucket+strategy+symbol, which is why 15 NIFTY-100 overlaps had to be dropped from the broad Midcap150+Smallcap100 set or they would double-enter. Capital is a shared FCFS budget across sets.

nodes.label: Circuit filter - 'F&O underlying OR hard band >=20%'
nodes.rationale: The obvious 'band >= 20%' test was actively WRONG: only 2 of 99 NIFTY-100 names have a 20% band because 97 are F&O with a dynamic band, so a width filter would have rejected the validated universe.

nodes.label: Per-scrip leverage via /v2/margincalculator, never predicted
nodes.rationale: Broker.required_margin asks Dhan for the answer and the runner fits size to it, degrading to 1x when unavailable. Product is per-ORDER (one Dhan account = one adapter): swing uses MTF, intraday uses INTRADAY with NO CNC fallback, because a CNC fallback would turn a 5x same-day trade into a 1x overnight delivery. Real median leverage (~4.4x N100 / ~3.1x smallcap) is below the backtest's assumed 5x, so expect lower return-on-margin.

nodes.label: Shared on-disk / Postgres Dhan token cache
nodes.rationale: Every process mints independently, so a restart or back-to-back runs cold-start into the 2-min cooldown with no token (27/99 symbols dropped). One 24h token is now shared by bot, dry-run and prepare via a 0600 gitignored cache, and dry-run scripts read it so they do NOT evict the live bot's session.
